Now I understand the structure better. For left alignment `<`:
- The pattern becomes `s + fill*` where s is the captured group
- So if we have `{:<}` and fill is space, it becomes `(.+?) *`

For search, this means after matching, the regex engine's `m.end()` will be at the position after all the trailing spaces (if there are any). This advances the iterator too far.

The fix for R9 should modify how the search position advances when there's padding involved. Specifically, for left and center aligned fields in a search context, we should stop at the next space character rather than consuming all padding.

One approach: After a match with alignment padding, adjust `self.pos` to not include the padding characters. We can do this by finding the actual end of the meaningful content.
